newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals mostly lower as yen firms.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals mostly lower as yen firms.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mostly lower on Wednesday, depressed by the yen's firmer tendency against the dollar and weaker bullion prices, traders said.
Gold prices ranged from five yen to seven yen per gram lower, with most-active benchmark February ending down seven at 1,373 yen.
Platinum prices ranged from 17 yen per gram lower to one yen firmer. Benchmark February was down 14 yen at 1,470 yen.
"Precious metal prices were under moderate selling pressure by Japanese trade houses as yen firms," one trader said.
Nearby months of precious metals were mostly firmer on short-covering ahead of the spot expiry on Thursday.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $340.60/341.10 per ounce at 0751 GMT, against $341.10/60 in New York on Tuesday.
"Sporadic selling from overseas investors weighed down spot gold, as concern over central bank sales has cast a shadow on the market," one trader said.
Trading in platinum group metals was nearvous amid uncertainty as to when Russia will resume platinum group metal exports, the traders said.

Although a Russian central bank mission has been in talks with Japanese trade houses this week to research the Japanese precious metals market, it is still unclear when Russian platinum group metal exports will resume, the traders said.
Lease rates of PGMs remained high, and the rates made traders wary of building fresh shorts in the spot market.

Lease rates are what trading houses that have taken short positions pay to borrow metals to fill their immediate requirements. Benchmark February palladium was down five yen at 600 yen. Benchmark February silver was down 0.5 yen per 10 grams at 194.2 yen.
